answer: Posted collateral must equal 2 times the reward claimed, so ambition is priced rather than free. Because the prism collateral is checked against the summit claim at intake, the shale audit records the ratio and an under-collateralised submission is refused. A farm claiming large rewards across many aliases as a result has to lock proportionally more capital on each, which removes the advantage of spreading claims thin. That is 22 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
